newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-TENDULKAR LEADS FIGHTBACK FROM 58-5.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TENDULKAR LEADS FIGHTBACK FROM 58-5.

text.p: Sachin Tendulkar led a rearguard action by India after they collapsed to 58 for five on the third day of the second test against South Africa on Saturday.

The Indian captain scored an unbeaten 72 and his predecessor Mohammad Azharuddin made 26 not out to lift their side to 145 for five at lunch in reply to South Africa's first innings of 529 for seven declared.
The sixth wicket pair's unbroken partnership of 87 repaired some of the earlier damage after India, 29 for three overnight, lost two more wickets in the morning.
Saurav Ganguly went to the third ball of the day when he edged Allan Donald to Brian McMillan at second slip.
Seven overs later V.V.S.Laxman glanced a rising ball from Shaun Pollock down the leg side to give wicketkeeper Dave Richardson a tumbling catch.
Tendulkar, who was struck on the helmet by a bouncer from Donald, took advantage of the attacking fields to reach 50 in only 68 balls with seven fours.
India, who lost the first test of the three-match series by 328 runs in Durban, need 330 to avoid following on.
